clue.text: Journalists riding to get exercise

parts.note: the press is the collective name for journalists
riding high is being up, as on horseback, so riding gives UP

explanation.surface: Reporters cycle or ride horses as a way of keeping fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding' reads as horseback exercise, but it is just UP, as in 'up on a horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms, called a push-up in America.

clue.text: What came before fabulous second homes?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
fab is the informal short form of fabulous

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what preceded marvellous holiday houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What came' is padding that turns the clue into a question; the pieces are just PRE, FAB and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefabs were quickly assembled factory-built houses, put up in Britain after the Second World War.

clue.text: A person isolated before time fault

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: a fault is a defect or disruption, so the word time is knocked out of order here

explanation.surface: Someone cut off earlier, blamed for a time-related error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fault' rearranges TIME into MITE, which follows ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious recluse who lives apart from others.

clue.text: However, animation is an art form

parts.note: still can mean however or nevertheless
animation means liveliness or being alive, that is, life

explanation.surface: A remark that, nonetheless, cartoon-making counts as art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animation' suggests cartoons, but here it simply means being alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Still life is a genre of painting depicting inanimate objects such as fruit and flowers.

clue.text: Why he picks out his food?

definitions.text: Why he picks out his food?

parts.words: Why he picks out his food?
parts.note: a bird pecks at food; someone who picks at a snack is a little hungry, the reason for the picking

explanation.surface: Wondering why a man selects particular things to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: To peck is to pick at food, as a bird does, and the clue asks why he does it: because he is slightly hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is British informal for slightly hungry, wanting a snack.

clue.text: Track welcomes non-smoking supporter

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail left by an animal
NS is the abbreviation for non-smoking, as on hotel or train signs

explanation.surface: A railway line greets a backer who doesn't smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts NS inside SPOOR, between SPO and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor backs a person or event, usually with money, much as a supporter does.

clue.text: Rush around for early morning exercises in the senior common room!

indicators.note: in places these letters within the abbreviation

parts.note: SCR is the abbreviation for a senior common room, the staff lounge in a British college
a.m. marks the morning hours
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Dons dashing about doing dawn workouts in their college lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: AM and PE go between the C and R of SCR. A senior common room is the lounge used by staff at a British college or school.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run about quickly and playfully, like a child or small animal.

clue.text: Tree needed by cockney stocking-manufacturer?

indicators.note: cockney speech, the London accent, famously drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a hosier makes or sells stockings and socks

explanation.surface: A London stocking-maker needs some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their aitches, so HOSIER loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose pliable twigs are used for basket-weaving.

clue.text: Sailor's requirement for supports under the ocean?

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits under the other

parts.note: the sea is the ocean
legs support the body, or a table

explanation.surface: A sailor needs supports beneath the sea, perhaps for an oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' puts LEGS below SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs are the ability to keep one's balance and avoid seasickness on a moving ship.

clue.text: Wine, dry and English, getting award

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
TT means teetotal, so not drinking: dry

explanation.surface: A dry English wine wins a prize at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like describing the wine but means teetotal, TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: Mournful English supporter gets single bill

parts.note: a leg supports the body
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A sad English fan is handed a bill for one.
explanation.walkthrough: AC, short for account, stands for a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead, so sorrowful.

clue.text: Creatures that rut out of perverse naturalism

indicators.note: the letters of a word come out of a twisted, perverse jumble of another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Animals that mate come from a contrary kind of nature study.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R, U and T from NATURALISM and rearrange the remaining NAALISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals are living creatures, as opposed to plants.

clue.text: Water spirit for noisy receiver

indicators.note: noisy means heard, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: an aerial receives radio or television signals

explanation.surface: A water spirit stands in for a crackling radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: AERIAL and the name of the sprite are near-identical when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the sprite in Shakespeare's The Tempest, and the name of a mermaid in a well-known film.

clue.text: Tense because it's defective

definitions.meaning: a verb tense: the past tense describing ongoing action

explanation.surface: Someone is on edge because something is faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is a grammatical tense for continuing past action, and imperfect also means flawed.

clue.text: Journalist taken in by posh language

indicators.note: being taken in means being received inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: swish is informal for smart, fashionable or posh
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is fooled by an upper-class language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived, but it puts ED inside SWISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedish is the language spoken in Sweden.

clue.text: Sally is about to accept one job

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral for one
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally is about to take on a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but means a witty retort; 'to accept' puts I and POST inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty remark, and a riposte is a sharp reply.

clue.text: How to secure an attachment?

parts.note: reads like advice on emotional bonding or email, but means fastening extra sheets to a document

explanation.surface: A question about forming a close bond or sending a file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attachment' suggests affection or an email file; here it is pages clipped together.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper clip is a bent-wire fastener for holding sheets of paper together.

clue.text: The late developing sportsman?

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: A late-blooming player who matures afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges THE LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, especially track and field.

clue.text: Medicine or hallucinogen given to worker?

indicators.note: something given to another is added to it, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a worker ant is the usual crossword worker
acid is slang for the drug LSD

explanation.surface: A drug or a trip handed to a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: ACID is given to ANT, so it follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid is a remedy that neutralises stomach acid to relieve indigestion.

clue.text: Flight attendant's way to wear new shoes?

indicators.note: wearing something means having it around you, so it holds the other letters
new means remade, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: How a stewardess wears fresh footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SHOES into HOESS; 'to wear' puts ST inside it, after HO.
explanation.definitionFit: An air hostess is a stewardess who looks after passengers on an aircraft.

clue.text: Egghead with question about king's attendant

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of egg

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: a query is a question
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An intellectual asks a question about a royal servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' means a brainy person but is read as the head of egg, E; 'about' puts QUERY around R.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer who attends a member of the British royal family.

clue.text: Drive back for engineers with evidence of life

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a pulse shows that someone is alive

explanation.surface: Engineers drive back, proving they are alive.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to drive it back or repel it.

clue.text: Wine substitute?

definitions.meaning: a wine set aside and aged before release
a player kept back to replace another

explanation.definitionFit: Reserve wine is aged longer before sale, and a reserve is a stand-in player.

clue.text: Chicken drumstick warning

parts.note: a drumstick is the leg of a cooked fowl
a car horn sounds a warning

explanation.surface: A chicken leg comes with a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drumstick' suits the chicken surface, but gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leghorn is a breed of domestic hen, named after the Italian port Livorno.

clue.text: A tsetse fly lands!

indicators.note: fly can mean move wildly, so the letters scatter and rearrange

explanation.surface: An African insect comes in to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect in apposition but rearranges A TSETSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large areas of land owned by one person, so landed properties.

clue.text: Smack your friends — where's the sense there!

definitions.note: the definition points to the place in the mouth where one of the five senses works

parts.note: a smack is a slight flavour or taste
buds is informal for friends

explanation.surface: Hitting your pals: what sense is there in that?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' suggests a slap but means a taste, as in 'a smack of garlic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste buds are the organs on the tongue through which flavour is sensed.

clue.text: Go in for record

definitions.meaning: to come inside or step into
to write down in a register

explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come into a place, and also to note something in a ledger or log.

clue.text: Legal claim of political wing

explanation.surface: An entitlement belonging to a party faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A right is an entitlement in law, and the Right is the conservative side of politics.

clue.text: A rector may become his servant!

definitions.text: A rector may become his servant!

indicators.note: one thing becoming another means a change of form, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: A clergyman can turn into the servant of God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may become' rearranges A RECTOR, and a rector is indeed the servant of the maker of all things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creator is God, the maker of the world, whom a clergyman serves.

clue.text: Launch of new design — cylinder revealed

parts.note: a roll is a cylindrical shape, as of paper
out means disclosed or no longer secret

explanation.surface: A new product unveils its cylindrical shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' gives OUT, as when a secret is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the official introduction of a new product or aircraft.

clue.text: Modest royalties mean embracing ruin

indicators.note: the words hold the answer in their arms, so it runs across them

explanation.surface: Small earnings from writing spell ruin for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' is a link: the words mean the answer; the run sits across the word break of the two clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to wreck or ruin completely.

clue.text: Grows pot in former outskirts of dumfries

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the others

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: Someone raises plants in pots on the edge of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN goes between EX and DS. Dumfries is a town in southwest Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that expands grows larger or swells.
